holidays.name: National Candy Day
holidays.description: A sugar-fueled celebration where people are encouraged to indulge in their favorite sweets, from gummy bears to chocolate bars, the day after Halloween leaves everyone's pantry overflowing with leftover treats.
holidays.origin: Often credited to Albanese Candy, which has promoted National Candy Day on November 4 since the early 2010s, partly to give Halloween leftovers a proper send-off.
holidays.funFact: Americans buy billions of dollars worth of candy each year, and a big share of that haul happens around Halloween, which is why November 4 is prime time for discount candy shopping.

holidays.name: National Chicken Lady Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate the people who keep backyard chickens, talk to them like family, and proudly hand out eggs to neighbors. Wear your feathered-friend pride with flair.
holidays.origin: An informal observance that sprang from the growing backyard poultry movement and social media chicken fandom, honoring chicken keepers and their flocks.
holidays.funFact: Chickens can recognize over 100 different faces of other chickens and even some humans, so your flock really does know who you are.

holidays.name: Use Your Common Sense Day
holidays.description: A day to put down the instruction manual and rely on good old-fashioned common sense, like not microwaving metal or sticking forks in toasters. Warning labels everywhere get a day off.
holidays.origin: An unofficial observance that appears on many quirky holiday calendars, intended as a gentle reminder to think before acting.
holidays.funFact: Real product warning labels have included gems like 'Do not use hair dryer while sleeping' and 'Caution: Contents may be hot' on coffee cups, which is partly why this day is such a punchline.

holidays.name: King Tut Day
holidays.description: A day that commemorates the 1922 discovery of the entrance to Tutankhamun's tomb, which kicked off a worldwide craze for all things ancient Egyptian, including curse legends and golden masks.
holidays.origin: On November 4, 1922, British archaeologist Howard Carter's team found the first step leading down to the tomb of Pharaoh Tutankhamun in Egypt's Valley of the Kings.
holidays.funFact: The so-called 'Curse of the Pharaohs' was largely a newspaper invention, but it inspired decades of horror movies and even a 1978 Steve Martin novelty song called 'King Tut'.

holidays.name: National Waffle Day (Observed in Some Calendars)
holidays.description: A day to drown crisp, golden waffle squares in syrup, whipped cream, and fruit, or go savory with fried chicken and hot sauce. Every little pocket is an engineered syrup reservoir.
holidays.origin: While the more widely accepted National Waffle Day is August 24 in the U.S., some food calendars list waffle-related celebrations in early November as part of the comfort-food season.
holidays.funFact: The waffle iron was patented in the U.S. in 1869 by Cornelius Swarthout, and Thomas Jefferson reportedly brought waffle irons back from France.
